entities.summary: Numenius of Apamea was a Greek philosopher who lived in Rome and flourished during the latter half of the 2nd century AD. He was a Neopythagorean and forerunner of the Neoplatonists. His philosophical ideas were heavily influenced by the works of Pythagoras and Plato. He was a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of the time, and his writings had a significant impact on the development of Neoplatonism. Numenius' philosophical system was characterized by its emphasis on the unity of the universe and the interconnectedness of all things. He believed that the human soul was immortal and that the goal of human life was to attain spiritual enlightenment. Numenius' ideas were influential in the development of Western philosophy, particularly in the areas of metaphysics and epistemology. He is considered one of the most important figures in the history of Neoplatonism, and his writings continue to be studied by scholars today. Despite his significance, Numenius' life and teachings are not well documented, and much of what we know about him comes from the writings of later philosophers. Nevertheless, his legacy continues to be felt in the world of philosophy, and his ideas remain an important part of the Western philosophical tradition.
